subject: Media Literacy
title: Building a Trusted Information Diet
description: A 60-second lesson on Building a Trusted Information Diet.

hook.text: A man curated five reliable news sources and cut social media news. His accuracy on current events doubled.

buildup.text: An information diet means deliberately choosing which sources you consume rather than letting algorithms decide.

discovery.text: Key ingredients include diverse perspectives, established outlets, specialist sources, and fact-checking sites.

twist.text: Most people consume information passively — whatever the feed serves. Active curation takes effort but rewards accuracy.

climax.text: You curate what you eat. Curating what you read is just as important for your intellectual health.

punchline.text: Choose your sources like you choose your food. Quality matters more than quantity.

quiz.question: What is an 'information diet'?
options: Deliberately choosing which sources you consume rather than relying on algorithms
